title: How Marijuana Works
summary: Josh Clark and Chuck Bryant give a broad overview of marijuana (cannabis): its long history from ancient China and Egypt through its use as industrial hemp in America, the early twentieth-century criminalization (Marihuana Tax Act, Harry Anslinger, Reefer Madness), mandatory sentencing shifts through the Reagan era, and the modern legalization push in Washington and Colorado. They explain the cannabis plant (indica vs. sativa, male vs. female flowers, trichomes, THC), how THC affects the endocannabinoid system and brain regions like the hippocampus, cerebellum, and amygdala, the differences between smoking and eating (liver metabolism to 11-hydroxy-THC), drug testing detection windows, addiction debate, medicinal uses (glaucoma, nausea, appetite, epilepsy, MS, pain, cancer research), potency trends since the 1960s and 1970s, methods of consumption, lung health studies, and listener mail from an Australian volunteer firefighter.

segments.title: Opening banter and setting up the topic
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck open the show, thank guest producer Noel, and set the plan to cover marijuana's history, science, and social impact, with a joke about slang terms.

segments.title: Ancient history of cannabis and indica vs. sativa
segments.summary: Cannabis use in ancient China (Shen Nung), Egypt, and the Arabian Nights; theories about its origin; botanical debate over species; and the differing effects of indica (body high) and sativa (brain high), plus hybrid strains.

segments.title: Hemp and marijuana in early America
segments.summary: Hemp was widely grown in America and even required by Virginia law in 1619; the hosts discuss whether Founding Fathers smoked pot, and how Mexican immigrants after 1910 and racially charged reporting fed the vilification of marijuana.

segments.title: Propaganda, the Marihuana Tax Act, and Harry Anslinger
segments.summary: Newspaper panic stories, the word marijuana as a derogatory term, the film Reefer Madness, the 1937 Marihuana Tax Act, the role of Harry Anslinger, and the LaGuardia report that contradicted the fearmongering.

segments.title: Sentencing shifts from the 1950s through the Reagan era
segments.summary: Strict 1950s mandatory minimums, the 1960s relaxation and federal reports, the gateway drug debate, the 1970s decriminalization push and Nixon's opposition to the Shafer Commission, and Reagan-era laws including plant-versus-weight sentencing and LSD weight sentencing.

segments.title: Street prices and dispensary culture
segments.summary: Typical pot prices by weight (quarter ounce, ounce, pound), how dealers and dispensaries resemble each other, and licensed growers who were previously illegal.

segments.title: Cannabis plant anatomy and THC
segments.summary: The palmate leaf, sinsemilla female flowers, males being removed by growers, pollen spread, hermaphroditic plants, the hundreds of chemicals including over a hundred cannabinoids and about thirty-three carcinogens, THC as the main psychoactive compound, and trichomes where THC is stored.

segments.title: How smoking THC affects the brain and body
segments.summary: Following THC from the lungs into the bloodstream using farmer Ted as an example; paranoia and indica vs sativa; CBD counteracting paranoia; the endocannabinoid system discovered after THC was isolated in the 1960s; effects on hippocampus, cerebellum, basal ganglia, amygdala, hypothalamus, and dopamine; and how long effects and drug tests last.

segments.title: Eating marijuana, addiction, and medical uses
segments.summary: Oral ingestion is metabolized in the liver into a stronger, longer-lasting psychoactive compound, explaining delayed effects in Amsterdam. Addiction is debated, with withdrawal symptoms such as anxiety and insomnia. Medical uses include glaucoma, appetite and nausea in chemotherapy and AIDS, epilepsy (marijuana oil in Georgia), MS spasms, pain and inflammation, and cancer research, plus the Schedule I classification.

segments.title: Legalization momentum and potency trends
segments.summary: Public support for legalization, Washington and Colorado votes, the New Yorker article on Washington's legal market, the debate about 1960s-70s potency, University of Mississippi data showing average THC rising from 3.4% to 8.8% (2008 onward), and the potential for lower-potency products.

segments.title: Methods of consumption, lungs, and smoking studies
segments.summary: Joints, blunts, spliffs, pipes, bongs, vaporizers and e-cigarette cartridges; pop culture references; teen use rising after The Chronic; comparison of tar from marijuana and tobacco; University of Alabama at Birmingham study finding low to moderate pot use less harmful to lung function than tobacco; Marinol mention.

segments.summary: Andrew from Australia writes that the wildfire episode inspired him to join the Rural Fire Service and aim to become a smoke jumper.
